## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

This 1-fascicle text by [安玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E7%8E%84) Ān Xuán (the Eastern-Hàn lay-Buddhist translator) is the earliest Chinese version of the *Ugra-paripṛcchā* — the *Mahāyāna sūtra of the Inquiry of Ugra*, one of the foundational texts of bodhisattva-path doctrine. Ān Xuán was a contemporary collaborator of [安世高](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E4%B8%96%E9%AB%98) Ān Shìgāo and [支婁迦讖](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E5%A9%81%E8%BF%A6%E8%AE%96) Lokakṣema in the late-Hàn translation circle.

**Abstract**

The translation is conventionally datable to [安玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E7%8E%84) Ān Xuán's translation activity at the late-Hàn capital, c. 181 – 188 CE. The bracket adopted here reflects this window. The work is one of the most consequential bodhisattva-path texts in Buddhist canonical literature; modern scholarship (Nattier 2003) has substantially reassessed the *Ugra-paripṛcchā* as a foundational document for the early Mahāyāna movement.

The Taishō text (T0322) is established on the standard apparatus.
